hints.content: A relative maximum point is a point that is higher than all other graph points around it. It's like the highest point on a "peak."

The graph has two relative maximum points in the given section. One at $(-5,6)$, and one at $(7,-1)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes each scale by one. A function is made up of line segments and curved lines. The function starts at negative eight, three and increases at a non linear rate to negative five, six. Then it decreases at a non linear rate to zero, negative one-half. A line segment connects zero, negative one-half to two, negative seven. Then the function increases at a non linear rate to seven, negative one. Then the function decreases at a non linear rate to eight, two.
